key_developments.event: Hugh de Payens and eight companions found the Order at the Temple Mount in Jerusalem.
Council of Troyes officially recognizes the Order; Bernard of Clairvaux writes In Praise of the New Knighthood.
Bull Omne datum optimum exempts the Order from episcopal authority.
Battle of Hattin — Templar leadership decimated by Saladin.
Fall of Acre; Templars lose Levantine base.
Friday 13 October — mass arrest of French Templars by Philip IV.
Council of Vienne dissolves the Order.
Jacques de Molay burned at the stake in Paris.

_quarry.description: The Order of the Poor Knights of Christ and of the Temple of Solomon, founded c.1119 to protect Latin Christian pilgrims in the recently-captured Jerusalem. Granted papal exemption from local episcopal authority (Omne datum optimum, 1139), the Templars accumulated lands, banking networks, and a sophisticated proto-banking apparatus that financed the Crusader states. After the fall of Acre (1291) ended their Levantine raison d'être, Philip IV of France — heavily indebted to the Order — orchestrated their suppression. Mass arrests in 1307, dissolution by the Council of Vienne in 1312, and execution of Grand Master Jacques de Molay in 1314 ended the Order; its lands were largely transferred to the Hospitallers.
